title: Enhancing Scalability and Performance in Influence Maximization with Optimized Parallel Processing
problem: Influence Maximization (IM) is NP-hard and current approximate solutions like IMM do not scale efficiently on shared memory systems with multiple NUMA nodes. Optimizing parallelization and memory access patterns for many-core NUMA systems remains a key challenge.
motivation: Influence Maximization is critical for viral marketing and biological network analysis to identify key influencers in large networks.
method: EFFICIENTIMM targets the bottleneck in parallelizing influence maximization on computers with multiple processor cores and separate memory regions (NUMA nodes): cores have to access memory that might be located far away, causing them to stall. The solution combines four techniques: redesigning how work is divided among cores, placing data close to the cores that use it (optimizing memory affinity across nodes), spreading work evenly across cores and memory regions so all cores stay busy (load balancing), and having data structures adapt to runtime conditions. By eliminating slow memory access and keeping cores equally loaded, the algorithm runs much faster on these systems.
key_novelty: The key insight is combining memory-aware data placement, dynamic work distribution, and adaptive data structures as an integrated system to parallelize influence maximization.
contributions: New parallelization scheme for IMM optimized for shared memory architectures
NUMA-aware memory allocation and access pattern optimization
Dynamic load balancing strategy for multi-core NUMA systems
Fine-grained adaptive data structures for IMM
5.9x speedup over Ripples on SNAP datasets
primary_theme: parallel influence maximization with NUMA-aware optimization
